Write TRUE if the statement is correct and FALSE if the statement is not correct. (i) Abraham was originally from the land of Egypt. (ii) Sarah was the half sister of Abraham. (iii) God changed the name of Sarai to Sarah. (iv) Lot was saved from the destruction of Sodom. (v) The wife of Lot turned into a pillar of salt. (vi) Abraham lied to Pharaoh saying Sarah was his sister. (vii) Ishmael was the heir of the promise. (ix) Abraham was tested by God to sacrifice his only son. (x) Rebekah was the sister of Laban. (xi) Abraham died at the age of 175 years. (xii) Keturah was the second wife of Abraham. (xiii) Isaac was a twin. (xiv) Esau was a man of the field and a hunter. (xv) Jacob was the favorite son of Isaac. (xvi) Abraham had eight sons in total. (xvii) The covenant with Abraham included the promise of many descendants. (xviii) Abraham built an altar at Bethel. (xix) God appeared to Abraham in the form of three men. (xx) Abraham pleaded with God to save the righteous in Sodom.

Give short answers to the following questions. (i) List three promises God made to Abraham in Genesis 12. (ii) Mention two reasons why Lot chose the plain of Jordan. (iii) In Genesis 15:5 God told Abraham to look at the sky. (a) What did God ask him to count? (b) What was the purpose of this illustration? (c) How did Abraham respond to this promise? (iv) Briefly explain why Sarah laughed when she heard she would have a son. (v) Identify the two cities that were destroyed by fire and sulfur. (vi) Describe the instructions Abraham gave his servant regarding a wife for Isaac. (a) Where should the servant go? (b) What should the servant not do? (vii) Name the place where Abraham went to sacrifice Isaac. (viii) State the significance of the name change from Abram to Abraham. (ix) Who were the parents of Rebekah? Page 5 of 6 Find this and other free resources at: https://maktaba.tetea.org Find this and other free resources at: https://maktaba.tetea.org (x) How did Rebekah help the servant of Abraham at the well?

Give short answers to the following questions. (i) Go from your country and your kindred. (a) Who spoke these words? (b) To whom were they spoken? (c) What did the person have to leave behind? (d) What was the ultimate goal of this journey? (ii) Do not lay your hand on the boy. (a) Identify the speaker. (b) Who was the boy being referred to? (c) Why was the boy about to be killed? (d) What did this act prove about the faith of Abraham? (iii) Describe the three items God used in the covenant ceremony with Abraham in Genesis 15. (iv) Mention two characteristics of the character of Sarah. (v) The Lord will provide. (a) What is the Hebrew name for this expression? (b) On what occasion was this said? (vi) List the names of the two sons of Lot born after the destruction of Sodom. (vii) Briefly explain the conflict between Sarah and Hagar. (viii) What was the significance of the cave of Machpelah? (ix) Mention two ways in which Isaac prefigures Christ. (x) What are three lessons we learn from the hospitality of Abraham?
